text: {"lessons":["I repeatedly sold winners for the pleasure of locking in gains, then bought Stock A and Stock E back at higher prices. I should sell only when the investment case changes, and require a fresh reason before buying back.","I let purchase price and the pain of admitting a mistake influence my decisions, as when I sold Stock E at a steep loss. Average cost is not a reason to hold or sell; I should judge each position by its prospects and risk from today.","My account value declined despite several profitable sales, and it kept slipping while I made no trades. I should review the whole portfolio regularly and act when the overall risk or outlook warrants it, rather than focusing on isolated trade gains or staying inactive by default."]}
